overall: The AG found the committee improperly held part of a September 25 executive session with the property seller present, produced insufficiently detailed minutes, and withheld a used document; no intentional violation was found.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the committee improperly met in executive session on September 25, including a portion attended by the property seller's representatives.
allegations.key_passage: Therefore, we find that the portion of the executive session which the Masons attended was improper, and the Committee violated the Open Meeting Law by holding a discussion in executive session that lacked a proper statutory purpose.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the September 25 executive session minutes were insufficiently detailed, listing topics without summarizing the discussion.
allegations.key_passage: We therefore find that the Committee violated the Open Meeting Law by failing to draft and approve sufficiently detailed minutes for its September 25 executive session.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the committee improperly withheld from the public a document (the seller's proposal packet) used during the September 25 executive session.
allegations.key_passage: We also find that the Committee cannot withhold from the public a document that was used by the Committee during the September 25 executive session.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the board violated the Rule of Necessity; the AG noted this is not an Open Meeting Law question and declined to review it.
allegations.key_passage: We note that, even if true, this allegation would not constitute a violation of the Open Meeting Law, G.L. c. 30A, §§ 18-25.

allegations.summary: Complainant urged that the violations were intentional; the AG declined to find intent.
allegations.key_passage: we find that the Committee’s actions were the result of a sincere misunderstanding of the Law’s requirements, rather than an intentional violation of the Law.

remedy: Immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law, with a caution that a future similar violation may be considered evidence of intent.
Within 60 days, amend the September 25 executive session minutes to include sufficient detail, using whatever means are available, including attendees' memories and notes.
Upon approval of the amended minutes, immediately release to the public the portion summarizing the part of the executive session the sellers attended.
List the sellers' proposal packet in the minutes as a document used at the meeting and make it available as a public record.
remedy_passage: We order the Committee’s immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law and caution the Committee that a determination by our office of a similar violation in the future may be considered evidence of intent to violate the Open Meeting Law.
